chunk_findings.detail: `stored_boot` promises to return `""` when no boot id was recorded and `observe_boot` promises that reading never raises, but it catches only `OSError`. If `.ddflow/local/boot` exists and contains invalid UTF-8 bytes, e.g. `b"\xff"`, then `Path.read_text("utf-8")` raises `UnicodeDecodeError`, which is not caught. In that state `observe_boot(repo)` propagates the exception and crashes the health pass instead of returning a result with `changed=False`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_boot.py:34-39

chunk_findings.detail: `observe_boot` conflates an unreadable previous marker with a missing one. If the marker file already contains the current boot id but is read-denied while still writable, e.g. file mode `0222`, then `stored_boot` catches `PermissionError` and returns `""`; with a readable current boot id this makes `cur != prev`, so `observe_boot` writes the marker and returns `changed=True` even though no reboot occurred. That can license a post-reboot recovery sweep from an unchanged/unknown previous state, violating the module’s stated “unknown is not no” / never-run-an-unlicensed-sweep requirement.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_boot.py:52

chunk_findings.detail: The new recovery kinds are resolved through the same generic mode loop as correction kinds, so a global mode override can make them `apply`. For example, with `override="apply"` (e.g. `ddflow health --mode apply`) or `[health].mode=apply`, `own.get(k, "inherit")` returns `"inherit"` for `LAPSED_ALIVE`, `READY_TO_LAND`, and `MERGE_INTERRUPTED`, and the loop returns `"apply"` for those keys. The added comment states these detectors have no apply correction and “never apply anything”; returning `apply` for them routes the health engine down an apply path for a detector that has no correction (or records it as applied) without `recover` performing the recovery.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/healthwatch.py:_modes

chunk_findings.detail: The `landed_unlogged` detector uses “branch head is an ancestor of `base`, and `base` has commits beyond the branch” as proof that a merge landed without being logged. That shape is also exactly what an empty or stale branch has. For example, an item has `branch = "feature/x"` created from `main` at commit `A`, but no commits have been added to `feature/x`; `main` then advances to commit `B`. `_merges` runs `rev-parse refs/heads/feature/x` and gets `A`, `merge-base --is-ancestor A main` succeeds, and `rev-list --count refs/heads/feature/x..main` returns `1`, so it appends `MergeHang(... landed_unlogged=True)`. This is wrong: `rev-list --count main..feature/x` is `0`, no work landed, and the branch is merely an empty/stale branch created from a commit already contained in `main`. The code never checks the empty-branch condition its comment says it excludes, so ordinary branches created from an older base, reset to base, or otherwise having no unique commits can be misreported as landed-unlogged merge hangs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/healthwatch.py:_merges

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to verify that a lane owing more than `merge` is not proposed to land, but it never calls `H.inspect` and only asserts that the constructed `Ready` object's `owed` attribute is truthy. chunk_findings.detail: When the marker is present but unreadable, the `except (OSError, UnicodeError)` branch returns `changed=False` immediately and never writes the current boot id. Given `.ddflow/local/boot` containing invalid UTF-8 bytes (e.g. `b"\xff"`), the first `observe_boot(repo)` leaves the marker corrupt. If the machine later reboots and `boot_id()` changes, the next call still reads the same invalid marker, catches `UnicodeError`, and again returns `changed=False`; the detector is permanently stuck and never licenses the intended post-reboot recovery. The docstring says `observe_boot` records the current boot id and that unknown is not no; when the previous value is unknown but writing is possible, it should still update the marker with `changed=False`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_boot.py:observe_boot

chunk_findings.detail: The new `landed_unlogged` check only requires the branch tip to be a strict descendant of `it.base_sha` and an ancestor of `base`. That still accepts an empty branch that was fast-forwarded/reset to the current base. For example, with `it.base_sha = A`, `it.branch = feature/x`, and `base = main` advanced linearly from `A` to `B`, if `feature/x` has no commits of its own but was simply synced to `main` so `refs/heads/feature/x == B`, then `fork != head` is true, `merge-base --is-ancestor A B` succeeds, and `merge-base --is-ancestor B B` succeeds. `_merges` therefore appends a `MergeHang(... landed_unlogged=True, head=B, base=B)` finding even though no branch work landed unlogged; the branch tip is just the base. The fix excludes the empty tip-equals-fork case, but not the empty synced-to-base case.

chunk_findings.detail: `_readies` only filters out owed gates that are not `"merge"`; it never requires `commits_ahead > 0`. chunk_findings.detail: The landed-unlogged branch is selected before considering `m.merging`. If a `MergeHang` is constructed with both `merging=True` and `landed_unlogged=True`—which the bool fields permit—`_merge_hangs` returns the landed-unlogged detail/fix (`"record merge and complete ..."`) and ignores that a merge is still mid-flight. chunk_findings.detail: `observe_boot` replaces `.ddflow/local/boot` with `Path.write_text`, which truncates the file before writing. If that replacement is interrupted after truncation (for example, the process is killed, or a transient disk-full/EIO write fails and space is later freed), the marker can be left empty. On the next call, `prev` is read as `""`, `cur` is the unchanged boot id, and the code treats that empty marker as a first sighting: `cur != prev`, it writes the marker, and returns `changed=True`. This fabricates a reboot from a corrupt/unknown previous marker and can license a post-reboot recovery sweep even though no reboot occurred, contrary to the module’s stated invariant that unknown is not no and that the detector must not report a reboot from an unreadable/unknown marker.

chunk_findings.detail: `_merges` reports any item worktree with `W.merging(wt) is True` as a `MergeHang`, without checking whether the item’s lease is still live or how long the merge has been in progress; the function does not even receive `now`. Because recovery detector kinds can be acted on by `recover` under SAFE_AUTO, this can classify an active merge as an interrupted/hung merge and license recovery while the merge is still being worked on.

chunk_findings.detail: If the previous marker is readable and contains an old boot id, but the current boot id differs and the attempt to persist it fails (e.g. `.ddflow/local` is read-only or the disk is full so `fsio.atomic_write` raises `OSError`), `observe_boot` returns `changed=False`. For example, with `.ddflow/local/boot` containing `"old-boot-id\n"`, `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id` containing `"new-boot-id\n"`, and a failing marker write, the boot id has definitely changed and the previous value was not unreadable. Returning false here tells the recovery engine that no reboot was observed, so pre-reboot pids may be treated as possibly alive, contrary to the module’s stated purpose that the first pass after a reboot can tell that earlier pids are dead. The write failure should at most prevent persistence; it should not erase a known boot-id change.

chunk_findings.detail: The cap added for recovery detectors is only applied when the kind is absent from `own`, so any explicit configuration entry for a recovery kind defeats the cap. For example, with `own = {"lapsed_alive": "propose"}` and `override = "apply"`, the loop computes `mode = override or ...` as `"apply"`, then skips `if mode == "apply" and k not in own` because `"lapsed_alive" in own`, and returns `"apply"`; similarly `own = {"lapsed_alive": "inherit"}` with `h.mode = "apply"` returns `"apply"`. Thus a global `--mode apply` or `[health].mode = apply` can make the health pass apply `LAPSED_ALIVE`/`READY_TO_LAND`/`MERGE_INTERRUPTED`, despite the comment that these detectors are capped at `propose` and have no apply correction.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/healthwatch.py:_modes

chunk_findings.detail: Given an item whose lease is dead/released, whose branch is ahead of the base, and whose item worktree currently has `MERGE_HEAD` (i.e. a merge is mid-flight), `_readies` still appends a `Ready` finding. The function skips live leases and passed merge gates, but it never checks the worktree’s merge state, even though `_merges` in the same change treats exactly that condition as `MERGE_INTERRUPTED`. For example, with item `T1` having no live lease, `branch="feature/x"`, `_ahead(...) == 3`, `missing=("merge",)`, and `it.worktree` pointing to an existing worktree where `W.merging(wt) is True`, `_readies` returns `H.Ready("T1", "(none)", 3, ("merge",), "feature/x")` while `_merges` also returns a `MergeHang`. That makes the health pass emit a `READY_TO_LAND` finding proposing a merge on a worktree that is already mid-merge/interrupted, which is wrong for the “ready to land” detector and can drive recovery toward the less-specific/incorrect action instead of the merge-interrupted path.

chunk_findings.detail: The module docstring states that “A read OR write failure clears `changed`”, but the implementation does the opposite when the marker values differ. Given a repo with an old (or missing) `.ddflow/local/boot` marker and a read-only `.ddflow/local` directory, `observe_boot()` reads a different current boot id, `fsio.atomic_write()` raises `OSError`, the exception is swallowed, and the function still returns `{"changed": True}`. A recovery engine that uses `changed` to trigger a post-reboot sweep will therefore report a reboot on every pass after a failed marker write, repeatedly licensing destructive recovery even though the new boot id cannot be persisted; in the missing-marker case it can fabricate a reboot from an unknown previous state.

chunk_findings.detail: `_merges` (and `_readies`) infer that a holder is dead only from `it.lease.live(now, cfg.lease.grace_s)`, without consulting the `alive` information already computed by `gather` or any boot-id check. Given an item whose lease has lapsed beyond the grace period but whose holder process is still alive—the `lapsed_alive` case this change is meant to distinguish—and whose worktree has `W.merging(wt) is True`, `_merges` still appends a `MergeHang` (and `_readies` can append a `Ready`). That contradicts the function’s own “only the UNAMBIGUOUS, holder-DEAD signal” requirement and can cause recovery to interrupt or propose landing a merge that is actively being resolved.

chunk_findings.detail: The new boot-marker write is made “best effort” by swallowing every `Exception`, but the boot marker is not merely cosmetic: the recovery detectors rely on it to distinguish a current boot from stale PIDs. If the working tree or `.ddflow/local` is read-only, `.ddflow/local` is a file instead of a directory, or the disk is full, `observe_boot` can raise `OSError`/`NotADirectoryError`; the handler silently passes and the MCP server continues with the old boot id still on disk. A health pass after a real reboot can then fail to recognize that the process/boot is newer than previously recorded PIDs, defeating the stated recovery behavior and potentially misclassifying stale PIDs; the same catch also hides programming errors such as a wrong argument type to `observe_boot`.

chunk_findings.detail: Both boot-id tests do `if not boot: return` when `W.boot_id()` is empty. If `W.boot_id()` regresses to returning an empty value on Linux (for example, unreadable `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`, wrong path, or stripped-to-empty logic), the tests exit before calling `W.observe_boot()` or `W.stored_boot()` and therefore pass without exercising the boot-id recovery path. A broken `observe_boot`/`stored_boot` implementation that never writes the marker or stores the wrong boot id could still get a green test run in that environment.

chunk_findings.detail: `observe_boot()` treats a missing boot marker as a proven first-sighting change even when the marker cannot be persisted. Given a repo with no `.ddflow/local/boot` and an unwritable `.ddflow/local` path (for example, a read-only filesystem, or a missing `.ddflow` under a read-only repo root), `m.read_text()` raises `FileNotFoundError`, `prev` becomes `""`, `cur != prev`, the `mkdir`/`atomic_write` attempt raises `OSError`, and the exception is swallowed, so the function returns `changed=True`. Because the marker was never written, every later call repeats the same path and returns `changed=True` again, so a recovery engine that uses `changed` to infer a reboot will see a reboot on every pass rather than once; the previous boot id is unknown, not proven to have changed.

chunk_findings.detail: `_readies` and `_merges` decide holder liveness only from `it.lease.live(now, cfg.lease.grace_s)`, even though `gather` already computes the `alive` map and the change introduces boot-id to distinguish a stale PID from a live holder. If an item has a lease that has lapsed beyond the grace period while its holder process is still alive on the current boot—the `lapsed_alive` case this change is supposed to separate from “crashed”—these new detectors treat the holder as dead: `_merges` appends a `MergeHang` whenever `W.merging(wt) is True`, and `_readies` can append a `Ready` when the branch is ahead and all non-merge required gates are satisfied. For example, item `1` with `branch="feature"`, a mid-merge worktree, non-merge gates satisfied, `lease.live(...)` false because the lease lapsed, but `alive["1"]` true: the code proposes an interrupted merge / ready-to-land for a live holder, which can cause a concurrent merge or cleanup of an in-flight merge. The earlier refutation probe only checked that `Item.gate_outcome`/`gate_satisfied` exist and that a health pass ran; it did not show that lapsed-but-alive holders are excluded, and the current code still does not pass or consult `alive`/boot-id in these new functions.

chunk_findings.detail: Both new liveness checks dereference `lease.holder` / `it.lease.holder` without guarding for a missing lease. In `_readies`, after `lease = it.lease`, a non-terminal item with a branch but no lease (the “released” lane the docstring explicitly mentions) falls through `if lease is not None and lease.live(...)` and raises `AttributeError` at `if check(lease.holder)[0] is True:`. chunk_findings.detail: The two new detectors are evaluated independently inside `gather`, so they can return contradictory findings for the same item when the worktree merge state changes between the two calls. Given an item with a dropped lane (no live lease, holder not alive), branch ahead of base, and all non-merge required gates satisfied, if `W.merging(wt)` is false while `_readies` runs but becomes true before `_merges` runs (for example, a merge starts in that worktree during the healthwatch pass), `_readies` appends a `Ready` finding and `_merges` appends a `MergeHang` finding. The code comment says “two detectors must not disagree about one item,” but the non-atomic filesystem reads allow exactly that disagreement; `H.inspect` deduplicates by finding key, not by item, so both findings can be surfaced.
